source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - Alex Rueter x Andrew Musial — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter named or referenced on the call. Nothing from an application was read back. The lead is inbound from an Instagram advertisement — 'I found one of his ads on Instagram' — and the prospect did not know Trevor's work at all beforehand: asked how well he knew it, he answered 'not at all actually.' Whoever booked the call set no price expectation.

prospect.name: Alexander Rueter
prospect.aka: Addressed as Alex by the rep
prospect.location: United States — not further specified; long car commute, works outdoors on municipal sports grounds
prospect.occupation: Parks and Recreation grounds manager — manages seven baseball fields and a handful of properties for landscaping. Physically active work: 'On any given day, I could be walking anywhere from five to ten miles.' Also operates spraying machinery. Schedule: up at 3am, out of the door by 5am, works 6am to 2.30pm, then a 30 to 50 minute drive home.
prospect.training_background: Essentially untrained now. Played tennis in high school and used the college gym while studying, then stopped after graduating and never re-established it — partly because the nearest gyms were too far: 'I'm too tired to go to the gym, I don't want to travel that amount of time to get there.' Recently restarted shoulder presses at home with free weights to rebuild shoulder strength after a dislocation. Was given at-home exercises by a physical therapist and has stopped doing them — asked directly whether he still does them, he answered 'Should be, but no.' Also had massage therapy that helped the joints until the therapist moved away, and chiropractic that gave about a day of relief at a time. Gym-averse for social reasons: 'I'm a little too shy to be working out in a gym. And also, the gyms around me, there's a lot of the social media people that are in there trying to get videos, and it's been uncomfortable.' Hobby: archery, used as stress relief.
prospect.medical: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a genetic connective tissue disorder — 'I have what's called EDS or Ehlers-Danlos syndrome' — with recurrent joint instability. Reconstructive elbow surgery in high school. Partially dislocated a shoulder about a month before the call, and partially dislocated it again a few weeks before while catching a swinging door: 'the rotator cuff and all the other stuff in the back here is not as strong or strengthened as it probably should be.' Weak and stiff hip flexors, which he links to lower back pain and knee pain; his kneecap subluxes when he walks more in warmer months — 'my kneecap does this like popping feeling, it's like dislocating a joint' — and it happens daily. Back pain severe enough after two days of spraying twelve acres that he needed ice each evening. Describes his weight as 'technically obese' at 220 lb and 5'11", though he says his primary care physician is not concerned given his activity level. Under chiropractic and physical therapy care. Has ADD and takes medication for it. Drinks alcohol rarely, at most once a month.

signals: Wants a former self back with a specific target and date: 220 lb down to 180-190 lb and a 36-inch waist down to 30 inches, weights he last held in college — 'That would have been 15, maybe even 20 years ago.'

Ground lost across a long hard season rather than one event: a genetic connective tissue disorder progressing, a gym habit abandoned after college, interventions that never stuck, and an accumulating stack of joint problems.

Visible regret and embarrassment, stated plainly: 'Embarrassed of having this gut hanging out front', 'I have to wear a 2XL just to wear a t-shirt when I'd probably, for my frame, be in a large', and 'I feel like I'm probably 10 years older than what I should be, comparative to my friends.'

Expects himself to quit, which is the avatar's characteristic self-doubt — asked what the devil on his shoulder was saying, he answered: 'Nothing demeaning, but just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts.'

COUNTER-SIGNAL, and the reason confidence is not higher: the_medically_constrained was seriously considered, since Ehlers-Danlos with recurrent subluxation may well be an injury the programme cannot safely work around. It was rejected because that avatar requires high intent and no price resistance, and here the price resistance is absolute — $40 of cash on hand. On the financial dimension he sits outside every avatar in the taxonomy, which are all drawn from a buying population he is not part of.

goals.text: Lose the belly — from a 36-inch waist to a 30-inch waist, and from 220 lb to 180-190 lb
Build core muscles — his literal answer to the six-month goal question
Be comfortable taking his shirt off at the pool or the beach — 'I just want to be comfortable. Not only do I work outside, but I play outside'
Get through the working day without pain, which he chose over appearance when forced to pick one
Build enough strength around the joints to stop dislocating them — after partially dislocating a shoulder catching a door
Come home with enough left to mow the lawn or shoot his bow instead of sitting on ice — 'just enjoy my life the way I want to'
Shoot more arrows before his form degrades — currently about two quivers, roughly 24 arrows
Train at home, because gyms are both too far and socially uncomfortable for him
Get a system and an understanding rather than more options — 'everybody has the internet, so you have all the opportunity, but I lack the understanding and the system to go towards'

pains.text: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome — a genetic connective tissue disorder producing recurrent joint instability across the whole body
Two partial shoulder dislocations in roughly a month, the second from catching a swinging door
Kneecap subluxes when walking, daily, and worsens as he walks more in warmer months
Weak and stiff hip flexors driving lower back and knee pain
Back wrecked by physical work — after two days spraying twelve acres, 'I was a wreck after each day having to get some ice on my back'
Prior reconstructive elbow surgery in high school
Self-described as technically obese at 220 lb and 5'11", wearing 2XL for a frame he thinks should be large
Embarrassment about his body — 'Embarrassed of having this gut hanging out front'
Feels far older than his peers — 'I feel like I'm probably 10 years older than what I should be, comparative to my friends'
Nothing has stuck: massage therapy ended when the therapist moved, chiropractic relief lasted about a day, and the physical therapist's home exercises were abandoned — 'Should be, but no'
Exhaustion from an extreme schedule — up at 3am, out by 5, working 6 to 2.30, then a 30 to 50 minute commute: 'I would say motivation, but also, I'm just tired, man'
Expects himself to quit again — the devil on his shoulder says 'just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts'
Gym-averse from shyness and from being filmed by other members
Severe financial distress — $40 of cash on hand, repaying a retirement loan over two years, a mortgage on a recently bought house with problems, and a credit card being paid down
Eats more carbohydrates than he wants to because they are cheaper — 'At the moment, money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper'
Strong sweet tooth — 'ice cream, cookies, you name it, anything sweet'

objections.raw_quote: I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.
objections.rep_response: Did not react to the surprise itself. He moved straight to isolation — 'just to make sure, finances side, because we can talk about numbers, are you, like, you feel confident that you actually can get to your goals with this?' — which was the right sequencing, but the fact that a prospect reached the price after fifty minutes with no idea of the order of magnitude was never acknowledged or escalated.

objections.raw_quote: I, the financial is where it's going to stop. Like, that is, I have no ability to change that at this point in time.
objections.rep_response: Ran Objection C properly and to conclusion. Isolated twice, reframed to should-versus-how ('you're not in a, let's say, should place, but, like, how to do it?'), opened the payment door, asked permission for an open financial conversation, and then took the picture: cash on hand ($40), how he lives on it, and credit cards ('Could, but I'm paying that off right now'). Having established the position he stopped rather than grinding, and pivoted to sending free materials.

objections.raw_quote: Currently paying back my retirement for an issue that I had in the house. And I've got my mortgage. So there's not much wiggle room. And the retirement will be paid off in two years. And then I've got the credit card. So I don't have a specific time for it.
objections.rep_response: Asked the right question — 'how do you feel when you said that you're gonna pay that off? Like, what's the timeframe?' — got a two-year horizon with no defined end for the credit card, and correctly did not push against it. He closed with 'I'll send you some materials that you can start working by yourself... and we can have another conversation in some time. I'm not giving up on you.'

objections.raw_quote: How about when I get to the financial point that I can do this? I did get Trevor's free follow along guide. And once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all. I have no problems with doing a little bit here and there. And then when I get to the point where I can pay the money, I'll reach back out to y'all. Because I understand that you still have to make money yourself, so no worries there.
objections.rep_response: Answered the apology rather than the substance, and did it well: 'Look, it's not about me. My life won't change if you're gonna buy or if you're not gonna buy. My life won't change. But yours, definitely, this is a life-changing moment.' He then agreed to the prospect's own proposal and extended it by offering to send further materials. Proposed label for this objection type: self_directed_interim_plan — a prospect proposing to use the free product until he can afford the paid one.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structure was ever named. The rep said only 'Most of the clients just take it upfront, but for some of them, it shouldn't be the way that they should proceed. I understand that. So we don't have any set payment plans. It's all customized depending on what's best for the client.' The financial picture that followed established there was nothing to structure. Note this is the same 'no set payment plans' formulation the rep used with Bruno on 25 May, and it contradicts both the structured plans he quoted to Marian Samson and João Dantas and the policy stated on the internal onboarding call.

prospect_financials.disclosure_notes: Verbatim: 'Only about 40, $40 cash on hand', and when probed, 'that's just what's for gas. I have groceries that I have scheduled out. So my mortgage is paid and my loans are paid.' Credit cards exist but are being paid down: 'Could, but I'm paying that off right now.' Also repaying a retirement withdrawal taken to fix problems with a recently purchased house, with a two-year horizon, plus the mortgage. Monthly surplus was not asked but is effectively nil on his own account.

evidence: Explicit and immediate refusal of both tiers on first hearing the price: 'I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.'
Confirmed as absolute rather than negotiable when isolated: 'the financial is where it's going to stop. Like, that is, I have no ability to change that at this point in time.'
The financial picture the rep then took confirms it independently: $40 of cash on hand, credit cards being paid down, a retirement loan with a two-year repayment horizon, and a mortgage.

No payment, no payment link, no verbal agreement, and no follow-up call was scheduled — only an open-ended intention: 'we can have another conversation in some time' and 'I'm not giving up on you... give me a few days and I will send you the materials.'

Counter-evidence, and it is why the confidence is 0.9 rather than higher: intent and belief were both fully established before the number. He confirmed 'yes' to the belief check, took personal responsibility unprompted ('Because I'm the only one that can help me'), and granted the rep permission to hold him accountable. He also proposed re-contacting Primal himself once his debts clear. This is a relationship that could reopen, but not on any timeline either party could name.
The prospect's own timeline for affordability was two years for the retirement loan and undefined for the credit card, so treating this as a follow_up would overstate it.
outcome.next_step: No call scheduled. The rep committed to sending free training materials within a few days and to staying in touch; the prospect committed to reaching back out when his debts are cleared. Nothing dated on either side.

notable.note: The best-executed process in the batch, run on a prospect who could never have bought, and the two facts together are the finding. PROCESS: this is the only call in the batch where the consequence frame, the commitment check and the money play all ran properly, and the money play is the textbook run — isolate, should-versus-how, permission, then cash on hand and credit — after which the rep stopped rather than grinding a man with $40 to his name. He then did something not in the playbook and worth recording: he sent the prospect away with free materials and 'I'm not giving up on you', having first refused the prospect's apology with 'it's not about me. My life won't change if you're gonna buy or if you're not gonna buy.' QUALIFICATION FAILURE: the prospect gave three explicit financial warnings before the pitch — 'money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper' at 00:07:39, 'a good amount of it right now has been due to my financial instability... just bought a house and then there was a bunch of issues with it' at 00:17:09, and, in direct answer to the go-all-in question at 00:31:12, 'Other than I'm curious on the financial side of it.' All three were passed over, and fifty minutes of closing time went into a $6,000 presentation for someone with $40. He also arrived with no price expectation at all, from an Instagram ad, not knowing who Trevor was: 'not at all actually.' CLINICAL: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is a genetic connective tissue disorder and this prospect subluxes a shoulder catching a door and a kneecap while walking. He is under chiropractic and physiotherapy care, and the rep — uniquely in this batch — actually asked about clinicians and about compliance with prescribed exercises. He then never asked whether either clinician would sanction loaded ballistic kettlebell work, and pitched it as the answer. Of every prospect in this batch this is the one where the missing clinical screen carries the most physical risk. NUTRITION: the pillar prescribed meat, eggs, vegetables and fruit to a man who had already said he eats cheap carbohydrates because money is tight. The cost of the prescribed diet was never addressed. ICP: he is very close to the literal negative example in Primal's own stated ICP — 'dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight and I hate working out' — and he still received a full closer call.

quality.notes: Severe, and worse at both ends of the call than in the middle. The entire opening through 00:01:02 is a single undifferentiated block under the rep's label containing both the rep's frame and the prospect's first answer about EDS. The closing from roughly 00:53:41 to 00:55:01 collapses the same way, merging the rep's nurture offer with the prospect's replies. Individual inversions throughout: at 00:09:56 'How get back to this?' is split across labels mid-question; at 00:11:55 'And when you say feel comfortable, like' sits under the prospect but is the rep; at 00:16:44 the rep's own recap 'I think 15 years ago was the last time that you weighed like 180' lands under the prospect; and at 00:47:26 'Which direction feels better for you?' sits under the prospect but is plainly the rep, immediately before the prospect's 'You said six D, like six zero?' The pricing is nonetheless unambiguous from context — $6,000 for six months and $9,000 for twelve, confirmed by the rep's clarification 'For six months, it's $6K, $6,000.' The prospect's connection dropped several times, which he flagged himself ('my apologies if it cuts in and out. Apparently, my internet is acting funny'), and there are several passages of ASR noise ('talking almost thesis', 'my AED meds were awesome' for ADD meds, 'the counter-tractor' for chiropractor). The rep again carries the 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' label.
